principles: Host-neutral Lattice workflow identity must not be branded as a specific agent namespace.
Package identity, runtime lookup, hooks, and verifiers must agree on one canonical scope.
Legacy names should be retired from live execution paths without rewriting unrelated historical records.
drivers: Global lattice currently links through @lattice-agent/core, contradicting product naming.
pre-push still keys self-host detection on @koala-agent/core, silently skipping the intended gate.
Generated bootstrap and adapter checks can drift if only package.json is renamed.

options.name: A: Rename live scope to @lattice and update runtime/self-host checks consistently
pros: Matches product identity and host-neutral design.
Fixes the real package/global link correctness issue.
Keeps current CLI command surface unchanged while removing misleading npm scope.
cons: Requires coordinated package-lock, bootstrap, hook, and verifier updates.
Some historical docs will still mention old names, so acceptance needs an active-guidance boundary.

options.name: B: Keep @lattice-agent and only relabel docs
cons: Does not fix user-reported correctness issue.
Keeps Lattice conceptually tied to an agent namespace.

options.name: C: Add @lattice aliases while retaining @lattice-agent as canonical
pros: Could preserve backward compatibility with already generated installs.
cons: Encourages agents/hosts to keep generating stale guidance.
Violates the boundary that workflow commands and package identity should be host-neutral.

chosen: A: Rename live scope to @lattice and update runtime/self-host checks consistently
rationale: Choose A because the defect is a live canonical identity mismatch, not a documentation wording problem. A fixes the package manifests, runtime resolution, hooks, and verifiers as one consistent contract while avoiding arbitrary historical cleanup.

preMortem.scenario: Package manifests are renamed but generated bootstrap still searches @lattice-agent/core.
preMortem.trigger: A fresh init or worktree uses bin/lattice.js before local packages are built.
preMortem.consequence: CLI fails or falls back to stale global lattice despite package rename.
preMortem.mitigation: Update init-assets bootstrap candidates and verify-entrypoints assertions to @lattice/core.

preMortem.scenario: Global npm link still points to the old @lattice-agent/core package after code lands.
preMortem.trigger: User runs bare lattice from another host or retired Orchestrate root.
preMortem.consequence: The visible CLI remains branded through @lattice-agent/core and may use stale handlers.
preMortem.mitigation: After build, unlink old global package and link packages/main as @lattice/core; verify command -v lattice and npm ls -g.

preMortem.scenario: pre-push continues to skip self-host build+tsc because it checks the wrong package name.
preMortem.trigger: Developer pushes from proofbound after package rename.
preMortem.consequence: A type failure could bypass the local remote-write guard.
preMortem.mitigation: Change .githooks/pre-push self-host name to @lattice/core and verify script text plus relevant runtime verifiers.
